questions.prompt: Which situation most justifies behavior verification with a mock?

options.text: A pure function that returns a computed total
Code that must send an email when an order ships (no return value)

questions.explanation: When the interaction itself is the behavior and there's no result to check, verifying the call (an email was sent) is appropriate.

questions.prompt: How does assert_called_with differ from assert_called_once_with?

options.text: assert_called_with checks only the most recent call; assert_called_once_with also requires exactly one call

questions.explanation: assert_called_with inspects the latest call's args and ignores extra calls; assert_called_once_with additionally asserts there was exactly one call.

questions.prompt: To make a spy that records calls but still runs the real object, create it with `Mock(______=real_object)`.
questions.explanation: Mock(wraps=real_object) passes calls through to the real object while recording them for inspection.

questions.prompt: Which are signs of over-verification? Select all that apply.

options.text: Asserting the exact internal call sequence instead of the output
A test that breaks on a safe refactor even though behavior is unchanged
Checking every incidental helper call the code happens to make

questions.explanation: Over-verification pins incidental interactions and breaks on refactors; asserting the actual result/state is exactly what you should prefer.

questions.prompt: Match each unittest.mock feature to what it reports or does.

pairs.right: How many times the mock was called
Arguments of the most recent call
Arguments of every call, in order
Asserts the mock was never called

questions.explanation: These attributes and assertions let you inspect and verify the interactions a mock recorded.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to verify a required side effect with a mock.

items.text: Create a Mock for the collaborator
Run the code under test, passing the mock
Assert the expected call with assert_called_once_with

questions.explanation: Create the mock, exercise the code, then verify the interaction it should have produced.
